text:
carla: quick follow-up to the prefix cache RFC — proposing a "Graceful Departure Protocol" for prefixes when a node drains or we rebalance. goal: avoid transient cold misses and double-serves while keeping lease semantics simple.

ben: curious, what's different from the current handoff/evict flow?

carla: current flow is aggressive: mark demote + evict once tokens cleared. edgecases: inflight requests still hitting old owner, sequencer races, and short-lived leases cause flapping. this protocol staggers demote and adds a short guaranteed relay window.

alice: relay window = how long? we can't add too much tail latency.

carla: default 250ms-2s, configurable per tenant/priority. idea is: node A signals departure with a signed departure token + expected epoch. that starts a Relay phase where A will still serve reads for keys but will also forward any new writes/updates to the new owner B and to the global sequencer.

dan: so A acts as a relay/forwarder, not authoritative? how do we avoid double-apply?

carla: good Q. we keep authoritative writes gated by epoch comparison. A accepts reads if it has residency, but for writes it attaches its local epoch and the sequencer only accepts the write if epoch >= owner_epoch. we also pass a relay header so B can dedupe by operation-id.

sam: can you paste the rough handshake flow?

carla: sure — pseudo: 
```
# departure initiated on A
A -> sequencer: departure_request(prefix, target_owner=B, epoch=E+1, token=SIG)
sequencer -> B: assign_ownership(prefix, epoch=E+1)
sequencer -> A: departure_ack(prefix, relay_window_ms=250)
# Relay window starts
while relay_window not ended:
  A serves reads from cache
  A forwards writes to B with header: relay-from=A, op-id
# after window ends:
  A demote residency, drop cache; future reads go to B
```

ben: i like the op-id dedupe. needs stable op-id generation at the client layer though. what about KV prefetches? A might have cached values B doesn't yet.

carla: prefetches are treated as reads during relay; A can either respond from cache or fetch from backing store and forward resulting updates to B. key is to ensure B sees the same final state. so A forwards the resolved value + op-id. B applies idempotently.

alice: how do we ensure correctness under partial failures? e.g., A dies mid-relay?

carla: sequencer monitors health: if A fails before demote completes, sequencer short-circuits and forces B to fetch latest from store and increments epoch to avoid accepting stale relayed writes. we also have a small audit job that scans departure tokens and reconciles missed forwards.

dan: sounds heavy. what's the performance cost?

carla: additional forwarding on relays only for churn events (rebalance/drain). in steady state zero cost. relay window small. we trade a tiny amount of extra write traffic during moves for much fewer cold misses and smoother tail latency.

sam: rollout plan? feature flag per cluster?

carla: yes — opt-in via runtime flag. steps: unit tests + deterministic sim, small canary on dev cluster, chaos tests where A dies mid-window, then gradual ramp.

ben: one more nit: metricization. we should emit departure_forward_count, departure_forward_latency_p50/95, departure_reconcile_count, and stale-forward-detected.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add feature flag, add metrics, add sequencer ack path, add op-id header.

alice: also add e2e test that asserts no double-apply across ownership change (use op-id checker).

carla: agreed. i'll draft a short RFC follow-up with diagrams and simple failure-mode matrices. ping me if you want to pair on the sim harness. :thumbsup:

ben: +1 on drafting. i'd like a small prototype that logs op-ids so we can prove idempotency.

sam: tagging storage folks in follow-up RFC: @dan will you loop them?

dan: will do. starting a quick PR with the handshake proto sketch later today.

carla: thanks all — focusing on keeping demote semantics simple while reducing user-visible cold spikes.
